newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ridley buys Daco Canadian premix plants.
newsitem.headline: Ridley buys Daco Canadian premix plants.

text.p: Stockfeed producer Ridley Corporation Ltd said on Thursday it had bought two Canadian premix plants from Daco Laboratories Ltd.
"The acquisition will extend Ridley's coverage of the strategically important North American pig production markets," the company said.
The acquisition will be funded using a combination of existing credit facilities and equity in Ridley Corp.
idley said in a statement the Daco plants, located in Lethbridge, Alberta and Winnipeg, Manitoba, will be integrated with its Canadian-based Feed-Rite business.
The company said the acquisition would help position it to gain a share of significant feed markets in southern Alberta and the northern U.S. state of Montana.

The Daco premix plants manufacture concentrated nutritional base products for direct sale to livestock producers, who mix it with grain to produce a complete feed. The two plants sell about 6,000 tonnes of premix a year, providing the essential nutritional additives for about 210,000 tonnes of stockfeed.

"Taken in conjunction with our recently announced Hubbard Milling acquisition, which will virtually double the size of our North American stockfeed operations, the Daco business is a strategically important acquisition," Ridley managing director Gary Busenshut said in a statement.
Busenshut told Reuters the company had no plans to disclose the price of the deal.
Ridley, Australia's largest stockfeed producer, first entered North America with the acqusition of Feed-Rite in Western Canada in 1994.
Feed-Rite is currently being renamed Ridley Canada Ltd following Ridley's acquisition in April of the U.S. based Hubbard Milling.
That deal has now been completed, the company said.
